questions.question: How many fundamental duties are listed in the Indian Constitution as of 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Indian Constitution lists** **11 fundamental duties** as of** 2022, **which are outlined in **Article 51A of Part IV-A of the Constitution.**
 
• The 11th fundamental duty was added in 2002 by the **86th Amendment Act.**
 
• This duty mandates that parents or guardians provide educational opportunities for their children between the ages of six and fourteen.
 
• **The fundamental duties include**:
 
 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.
 
• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India, transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities, and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
• To develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement.
 
• To provide opportunities for education to one's child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years (added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002).

questions.question: In which of the following years did the government opt for a plan holiday after the seventh five - year plan?

__
 
• After the conclusion of the **Seventh Five-Year Plan in 1989**, India entered a phase commonly referred to as a** "plan holiday" from 1990 to 1992.**
 
• This period marked a deliberate hiatus in the traditional Five-Year Plans, which had been integral to India's economic planning process since its **independence in 1947**.
 
• The decision to pause the planning cycle was strategic, allowing the government to reassess its economic strategies and priorities without the constraints of adhering to an ongoing plan framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• During the **plan holiday**, India faced significant **economic challenges,** including severe fiscal deficits and imbalances in its balance of payments.
 
• These crises necessitated urgent measures to stabilize the economy and lay the groundwork for sustainable growth.
 
• In response to these challenges, the Indian government initiated far-reaching economic reforms, commonly known as the liberalization reforms of 1991.
 
• These reforms aimed to liberalize and open up the Indian economy, moving away from the centrally planned, state-controlled economic model towards a more market-oriented approach.

questions.question: Which of the following did NOT emerge as a result of disintegration of the Bahmani kingdom during the 16th century?

__
 
• **Gaur **did NOT emerge as a result of disintegration of the **Bahmani kingdom during the 16th century.**
 
• **The Bahmani Sultanate** was a significant **medieval Islamic state** in the **Deccan region of southern India**, which disintegrated into several smaller states known as the Deccan Sultanates in the early 16th century due to internal conflicts and external pressures.
 
• **The Gaur kingdom** was established in the Bengal region of eastern India during the **12th century,** much earlier than the disintegration of the Bahmani kingdom.
 
• It emerged as an independent kingdom under the rule of the Hindu Sena dynasty, which later came under the influence of Muslim rulers after the conquests of Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji in the 12th century.

• In **1518, the Bahmani Sultanate,** a Muslim empire governing the Deccan Plateau in South India, fragmented into five distinct sultanates, thus concluding its 180-year reign.
 
• These separate entities, collectively referred to as the Deccan Sultanates, are:
 
 
• **Ahmadnagar, **alternatively known as the Nizam Shahi dynasty.
 
• **Berar, **one of the constituent sultanates of the Deccan.
 
• **Bidar,** another sultanate within the Deccan region.
 
• **Bijapur,** also recognized as the Adil Shahi dynasty.

questions.question: Siachen in Himalayas is:

__
 
• **The Siachen Glacier,** situated in **the Karakoram-Himalayan region**, lies within the** eastern Karakoram mountain range,** close to the **borders of India, Pakistan, and China**.
 
• Stretching for **75 kilometers**, it ranks as the **second-longest nonpolar glacier** globally.
 
• Renowned as the **world's highest battlefield, **the Siachen Glacier gained this distinction due to its strategic location.
 
• In 1984, India launched a military operation to secure control over the glacier and its surrounding areas following attempts by the Pakistan army to occupy the region.
 
• Since then, India has maintained control over the glacier.
 
• Among the Karakoram's five largest glaciers, the Siachen Glacier sits at an average altitude of 18,000 feet above sea level, presenting a formidable and challenging terrain for military operations and exploration alike.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Glaciers** are fascinating natural phenomena formed by the accumulation and compaction of snow over long periods.
 
• As successive layers of snow accumulate, they undergo a process of transformation into dense glacial ice under the pressure of overlying snow layers.
 
• The weight of this ice mass, coupled with the force of gravity, initiates the movement of the glacier downhill and outward, a process known as glacial flow.

questions.question: Jagjit Singh is associated with which form of singing?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jagjit Singh**, renowned as the** "Ghazal King," **is celebrated for his association with ghazals, a **classical Persian song** form known for its **special rhyming patterns and stanzas** conveying themes of love.
 
• Credited with revitalizing the popularity of ghazals, Singh's work is considered genre-defining, making him the most successful ghazal singer and composer of all time.
 
• In recognition of his contributions, he was honored with the **Padma Bhushan** by the Government of India in 2003.
 
• Additionally, in February 2014, the government released a set of two postal stamps in his honor.
 
• Notably, Singh's rendition of Bahadur Shah Zafar's famous ghazal "Lagta nahin hai dil mera" at an event commemorating the 150th anniversary of the Indian Rebellion of 1857, held in the Central Hall of the Parliament of India on May 10, 2007, captivated audiences comprising numerous political and diplomatic luminaries.

• Typically, ghazals delve into themes of spiritual and romantic love, serving as a poetic expression of the complexities inherent in love, including the pain of separation from the beloved juxtaposed with the beauty of enduring love.
 
• Dating back to 7th-century Arabic poetry, the ghazal has a rich and ancient history.
 
• It found its way into the Indian subcontinent during the 12th century, influenced by Sufi mystics and the courts of the new Islamic Sultanate.

questions.question: When was the 8th round of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), the so-called ‘Uruguay Round’ which led to the establishment of World Trade Organization (WTO) completed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1994**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Uruguay Round**, the final installment of the **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), **concluded in April 1994 in Marrakesh, **Morocco.**
 
• This extensive negotiation process unfolded from 1986 to 1994, marking the largest international trade negotiation in history.
 
• The Uruguay Round was instrumental in establishing the **World Trade Organization (WTO),** which was founded in **1995 **and encompasses the principles of the GATT within a more comprehensive institutional framework.
 
• With **164 member nations** representing** 98% of global trade,** the WTO serves as a pivotal organization for regulating international commerce.
 
• Commencing in Punta del Este, Uruguay, on September 20, 1986, the Uruguay Round featured negotiations conducted across various global cities, including Geneva, Brussels, Washington, D.C., and Tokyo.
 
• The round spanned seven years and ultimately laid the groundwork for significant advancements in global trade governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)** is a binding legal accord among numerous countries, designed to diminish or eradicate trade impediments such as tariffs and quotas.
 
• Its overarching objective is to eradicate discriminatory practices in international trade.
 
• Initially signed in 1947 by 23 nations at the Palais des Nations in Geneva, the agreement experienced significant growth, with over 100 signatories by 1973.
 
• **The core objectives of the GATT are to**:
 
 
• Substantially diminish tariffs and other obstacles to trade.
 
• Eliminate preferential treatment.
 
• Achieve these objectives through reciprocal and mutually beneficial arrangements.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in inventory investment when calculating national income?

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution shall the executive power of the Union be vested in the President?

• **Article 53 of the Indian Constitution** outlines the executive authority given to the **President of India**.
 
• It states that the President holds this power, which can be exercised directly or through subordinate officers as per the Constitution.
 
• The President has s**upreme command **over the **Defence Forces**, regulated by law.
 
• This article also specifies that the President's powers do not override those already held by state governments or other authorities under existing laws, and Parliament retains the right to delegate functions to entities other than the President through legislation.

• **Article 56** of the Indian Constitution delineates the term of office for the President, stipulating that the President's term lasts for five years from the commencement of their term.

questions.question: From the given options, choose the one which is NOT a product of the decomposition reaction of Lead nitrate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nitrogen** is not produced as a** direct product of the decomposition reaction of lead nitrate. **
 
• When** lead nitrate **is heated, it undergoes decomposition into **lead oxide, nitrogen dioxide, and oxygen**. 
 
• The chemical equation representing this reaction is:
 
 
• **2Pb(NO₃)₂(s) → 2PbO(s) + 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g)**
 
 
 
• In this reaction, lead nitrate decomposes to form solid lead oxide and gases nitrogen dioxide and oxygen. 
 
• The **lead oxide** remains in solid form, while the** nitrogen dioxide and oxygen **are released as gases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A decomposition reaction**, also referred to as chemical breakdown, is a type of chemical reaction in which a single reactant molecule breaks down into two or more products.
 
• The general form of a decomposition reaction is represented as AB → A + B, where AB denotes the parent molecule or reactant.
 
• Decomposition reactions typically necessitate an input of energy, which can be provided in the form of heat, light, or electricity. Higher temperatures often facilitate the decomposition process, accelerating the rate of reaction.
 
• Depending on the specific reaction conditions, the overall process can either absorb heat from the surroundings (endothermic) or release heat to the surroundings (exothermic).

questions.question: Which of the following industries was NOT in Schedule A of Industrial Policy 1956?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mining of salt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mining of salt **was **NOT **in** Schedule A of Industrial Policy 1956.**
 
• Schedule A, consisting of **17 industries**, was exclusively under **the jurisdiction of the State**.
 
• Among these, **four industries arms and ammunition, atomic energy, railways, and air transport** were monopolized by the Central Government.
 
• **State Governments** were responsible for fostering the development of new units in the remaining industries.
 
• The industries listed in Schedule A were arms and ammunition and allied items of defence equipment, atomic energy, iron and steel, heavy castings and forgings of iron and steel, heavy plant and machinery required for iron and steel production, mining, machine tool manufacture, and other specified basic industries.
 
• Additionally, the schedule included heavy electrical plant, including large hydraulic and steam turbines, coal and lignite, mineral oils, mining of iron ore, manganese ore, chrome-ore, gypsum, sulphur, gold, and diamond, mining and processing of copper, lead, zinc, tin, molybdenum, and wolfram, minerals specified in the Schedule to the Atomic Energy (Control of Production and Use) Order, 1953, aircraft, air transport, railway transport, shipbuilding, telephones and telephone cables, telegraph and wireless apparatus (excluding radio receiving sets), and generation and distribution of electricity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956**, adopted by the Indian parliament in **April 1956,** marked a significant milestone in **India's industrial development strategy.**
 
• Following the **Industrial Policy of 1948**, it stood as the second comprehensive statement outlining the nation's industrial trajectory.
 
• Throughout subsequent** Five-Year Plans, the 1956** policy remained foundational, shaping India's economic landscape.
 
• Central to the resolution was the vision of establishing a socialist society, guiding social and economic policies towards this end.
 
• A key feature of IPR 1956 was the empowerment of governmental machinery, granting it enhanced authority in industrial matters.
 
• The resolution delineated three distinct categories of industries, each with its own delineated role:
 
 
• **Schedule A **encompassed industries deemed the exclusive responsibility of the state, highlighting the government's direct involvement and control.
 
• **Schedule B** identified sectors slated for progressive state ownership, where the government would establish new enterprises. Private enterprise was envisioned to supplement state efforts in these industries.
 
• **Schedule C** encompassed all remaining industries, where future development would predominantly be driven by private sector initiative and enterprise.

questions.question: The ________ birth rate indicates the number of live births occurring during the year per 1000 population estimated at midyear.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**crude**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The crude birth rate **indicates the** number of live births **occurring during the year **per 1000 population** estimated at midyear.
 
• The crude birth rate (CBR) represents the number of live births per 1,000 individuals in a population within a specific year.
 
• It's calculated by dividing the total number of live births during the year by the mid-year population and then multiplying by 1,000.
 
• This statistic, which is not adjusted for seasonal variations, serves as a key demographic and socioeconomic indicator.
 
• The CBR is instrumental in determining the** rate of natural population growth, excluding migration.**
 
• It's derived as a ratio, where the numerator is the number of live births within a defined time frame, and the denominator is the total person-years lived by the population during that period.
 
• Data on CBR is sourced from various channels, including birth and death registration systems, censuses, sample surveys conducted by **national statistical agencies **and other organizations, and demographic analysis.
 
• For example, in 2021, the United States recorded a CBR of 11.0 births per 1,000 people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Crude birth rate: Number of live births per 1,000 population: (Number of live births / Estimated midyear Population) x 1,000 **

• It primarily affects children in tropical and subtropical regions, particularly in areas with inadequate sanitation and hygiene practices.
 
• **Adult female Ascaris worms** can reach lengths exceeding one foot, while adult males typically measure between 15 to 30 centimeters.
 
• These worms inhabit the small intestine of their hosts, which include pigs and humans.

• **Taenia** is a genus of tapeworms that encompasses more than 100 species, responsible for causing cysticercosis and taeniasis in humans.

questions.question: Vultures are:

The correct answer is __C**arnivores**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vultures primarily feed on the flesh of dead animals, making them **scavengers** within the carnivore classification. They play a crucial ecological role by consuming carcasses that could otherwise spread diseases to other animals and humans.
 
• Their feeding behavior is specialized towards a carnivorous diet, as they have strong beaks and digestive systems capable of breaking down tough tissues and even handling bacteria that would be harmful to other animals.
 
• This makes them an essential part of the ecosystem, particularly in their role in naturally disposing of dead animals.

questions.question: What do you call the type of drugs that mimic natural messengers by switching on receptors?
questions.solution:

__
 
• In pharmacology, **agonists** are drugs or substances that mimic the **action of endogenous **(naturally occurring) molecules by binding to specific receptors in the body and activating them.
 
• These receptors are typically proteins located on the **surface of cells **or within** cells, **and they play crucial roles in transmitting signals and regulating various physiological processes.
 
• When an agonist binds to its receptor, it triggers a biological response similar to that produced by the **natural messenger **(endogenous ligand) for that receptor.
 
• This response can include changes in cellular activity, signaling pathways, or physiological functions, depending on the specific receptor and its location.

They typically work by increasing the levels of neurotransmitters like serotonin and noradrenaline in the brain, which can help regulate mood and alleviate symptoms of depression and anxiety.
 
• **Depressants or central depressants: **These drugs have the opposite effect of antidepressants. They lower neurotransmission levels in the brain, leading to a decrease in arousal or stimulation. Examples include alcohol, benzodiazepines, and barbiturates.

questions.question: The mean proportional between 0.03 and 0.0003 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Mean Proportional** (b) between two numbers a and c is √(a × c).

Given numbers: 0.03 and 0.0003.

⇒ Mean Proportional = √(0.000009)

⇒ Mean Proportional = 0.003

**∴ The correct answer is 0.003.**

**__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

For two numbers a and b, the third proportional c is calculated as a : b = b : c, which implies c = b² / a.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional d is calculated as a : b = c : d, which implies d = (b × c) / a.

Continued Proportion

Three numbers a, b, c are in continued proportion if a/b = b/c. This is the basis for the mean proportional definition.</p

questions.question: A boy goes from home to school at a speed of 30 km/h and returns back at a speed of 70 km/h. What is his average speed for the journey?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When the **distance** covered is the same for two different speeds, use the **Harmonic Mean** shortcut.

**Average Speed** = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 30 × 70) ÷ (30 + 70)

⇒ Average Speed = 4200 ÷ 100 = 42 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 42 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from **Home to School** (S₁) = 30 km/h

Speed from **School to Home** (S₂) = 70 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/053c50bf299dc039506c859d88e1dcde0ffd0f2ad9ee8e25d6078dec9024508d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the distance between Home and School be **210 km** (LCM of 30 and 70).

⇒ Time taken to reach school (T₁) = Distance ÷ S₁ = 210 ÷ 30 = 7 hours

⇒ Time taken to return home (T₂) = Distance ÷ S₂ = 210 ÷ 70 = 3 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 210 + 210 = 420 km

⇒ Total Time = 7 + 3 = 10 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 420 ÷ 10 = 42 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 42 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Different Distances

If a person covers distances d₁, d₂, d₃ with speeds s₁, s₂, s₃, then Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂ + d₃) ÷ (d₁/s₁ + d₂/s₂ + d₃/s₃).

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

If a person travels at different speeds for **equal time intervals**, the Average Speed is the **Arithmetic Mean**: (s₁ + s₂ + ... + sₙ) ÷ n.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p
